label: fs-substitution-holds-for-every-integrable-integrand
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The counterexample is built on the fat Cantor set, a closed nowhere-dense subset of $[0,1]$ with positive measure, and the functions $\varphi(x)=\int_0^x d_S$ and $f=\mathbf{1}_{\varphi[S]}$. The proof explicitly checks that $\varphi$ is strictly increasing (hence injective), that $\varphi[S]$ has content zero (hence null), and that the discontinuity sets of $f$ and $f\circ\varphi$ are exactly $\varphi[S]$ and $S$, respectively. All integrals are over nondegenerate closed intervals, and the use of Lebesgue’s criterion respects boundedness. No boundary case (empty, degenerate, endpoints) is mishandled.

SOURCES: All 39 declared cited items were provided in full and inspected. Every load‑bearing dependency (including the fat Cantor set definition, its positive measure, distance‑to‑set Lipschitz property, FTC first part, monotonicity of the integral, content‑zero implies null, and Lebesgue’s criterion) is correctly instantiated with its exact hypotheses. No hidden strengthening or weakening of a cited statement was detected.

CHECKED: The title, the false public claim (“continuity of $f$ may be weakened to integrability”), all 13 numbered proof steps, and the Remarks were verified. The construction successfully produces an integrable $f$ and a differentiable $\varphi$ with integrable derivative such that $f\circ\varphi$ is not Riemann integrable; the argument is mathematically valid and refutes the claim.
